That single moment changed what's considered possible in aerospace engineering.

🚨BREAKING: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr says the Biden FCC revoked Starlink’s $885 million award over 100/20 Mbps doubts

He now cites new Ookla data showing the benchmark was met by end of 2025 and says the decision slowed rural broadband efforts






Muskonomy (@muskonomy)

🚨BREAKING: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr says, “Under President Biden, the FCC revoked an $885 million award that Starlink won to provide high speed internet to millions of Americans.”

At the time, the agency argued that Starlink was unlikely to provide 100/20 Mbps service to 40% of required locations by the end of 2025.

Carr says he dissented from that decision, stating the record showed Starlink was on track and that the revocation was not consistent with the facts.

He now points to new Ookla Speedtest data showing that well over that percentage of Starlink users met the 100/20 Mbps benchmark by year end 2025 and argues the decision slowed efforts to close the digital divide and increased costs.

Falcon 9 is the only rocket in history that launches, lands and re-flies on a routine basis.

How it works:

The first stage separates from the second stage at altitude 
~ Engines reignite to slow the descent 
~ Grid fins steer it back to the landing zone or droneship 
~ Engines fire one more time for the final landing burn 
~ Touchdown is gentle enough that the booster can be inspected, refurbished and reused

This sequence happens 100+ times a year. Every other rocket family on Earth is single-use, even today, because nobody else has solved the problem.

NEWS: Greg Brockman confirms under oath that Sam Altman secretly paid him ~$10 million in equity from his personal family office in 2017, while OpenAI was still a nonprofit and Elon Musk had no idea.

The deal stayed hidden until Elon Musk's family office head Jared Birchall uncovered it. 

On August 18, 2017, Birchall wrote to Elon Musk: "He compensated Greg on the side… a percentage ownership of the LLC that holds the assets of Sam's personal family office, worth $10 million." H
e added: "Naturally, Greg is going to have greater allegiance towards Sam as a result of this arrangement."

Elon Musk forwarded the email to Brockman with one word: "??" Brockman never responded.

On the stand today, Brockman admitted Elon Musk "certainly didn't know about it." When asked if it was fair to keep a side deal with Sam Altman from his cofounder, Brockman said "We had never discussed compensation directly."

Asked why he didn't disclose that Sam Altman was personally compensating him while they were all running OpenAI together, Brockman's defense was: "Elon's time was relatively hard to get."

Two years before Sam Altman publicly offered Elon Musk equity in OpenAI, he had already privately bought Greg Brockman's loyalty for $10 million in equity, all while OpenAI was still a charity, and all hidden from the cofounder funding it.
